text:
Oil prices have pulled back this week—Brent crude dipped below $90 for the first time since August—on growing hope that the Iran conflict could wind down soon, with President Trump publicly suggesting it will "end fairly soon." For a refiner like this one, lower crude prices are a direct tailwind: they reduce the cost of the raw material the refinery processes. At the same time, refineries are running near full capacity at 95.2%, which means the company is converting that cheaper crude into fuel efficiently and selling into a market where gasoline and diesel inventories remain modest.

The longer backdrop here cuts both ways. Trump's midterm election loss has emboldened renewable energy advocates, which is a headwind for oil refiners over time. But the near-term momentum—cheaper oil, high utilization, and peace hopes—appears to be supporting the sector this week.
